meta.title: CivicOS experience inputs for UX design
readThis: Every line carries basis. 'fixed' means the canon or the approved module requirements say it, and src names where. 'open' means the canon does not settle it; the text is the question the design must answer. Nothing marked open has an invented answer.

Act references use the inventory's own names, written 'construct-id: Act name' (docs/development/ux-substrate/ux-substrate-v2.json). Screen inventory, act weights and working names are another worker's job and are not repeated here.

Two words mean two things. RUNG is how heavy an act is (reversible, reasoned, terminal, attested, irreversible). WEIGHT is how an act applied to a set behaves (refuse = all or nothing, report = proceed and say what moved, per-item = each applied or kept with its reason, single = one object). Source: affordances R1-R2; Interaction Constructs, naming collision corrected 2026-08-01.

'Finding' is overloaded: in case-making it is a concluded question; in the queue it is a class of item the record noticed and nobody has judged (inventory contradictions). This file says 'concluded finding' or 'queue finding' where it matters.
Coverage (useCases) says whether approved module requirements (build/requirements/*.md) hold the use case, not whether it is built.
Open questions carry a Bob-facing brief; settled ones carry a 'ruled' entry stating the design as it stands.

Where a line says 'decided' or 'decided, not built', Bob has ruled it but no approved requirement carries it yet; 'specified in T18' means the requirement is written and T18 builds it; 'built at the plane' means built with no member surface yet (the old interface, civicos-ui/app.html, is unchanged).

neededIntro: These are the decisions about what members see and do that only you can make. Each one opens to the decision in a sentence, why it is yours, the background with an example, what is already fixed, the choices with what each gains and costs, a recommendation, and a few ways you might answer. Take them in any order; the table shows which are quick.

To answer, reply with the number and your ruling, for example “15: as recommended” or “19: option B, but pseudonymous work shows the same strength”. A question is welcome instead of a ruling. Each ruling is recorded, folded into the design documents, and this page is updated in the same change.

useCases.name: Search the record
useCases.goal: Find documents, passages, questions and legs by typing one query language.
useCases.trigger: A member wants something already held.
useCases.outcome: Rows the viewer may see, with facets, a note of what could not be seen, and widening when an AND finds nothing.

useCases.name: Search outside sources in one query (city data, legal databases, other groups, news)
useCases.goal: One question fans out to heterogeneous public sources with provenance and trust on each result.
useCases.trigger: A member does not yet hold the material.
useCases.outcome: Results with provenance, recency and trust signals, accepted into the record.
useCases.requirementIds: ai-runs R9-R14 (FIND only inside a run); capture-requests R1-R22
useCases.src: Functional Architecture 'Search across heterogeneous sources'; AI Roles section 2 (standalone FIND ABSENT)
useCases.coverageNote: No module holds a standalone fan-out search over outside sources; FIND exists only inside an investigative run.

useCases.name: Assemble what is known about a focus area (Context skill)
useCases.goal: Surface relevant laws, reports, other groups' work and request status for an area of interest.
useCases.trigger: A group orients on a new area.
useCases.outcome: An assembled landscape the member reviews.
useCases.src: Functional Architecture Layer 1 skills; Roadmap sections 9-10 (Orient); inventory inFlux ('Discovery ... beyond MVP')
useCases.coverageNote: No module requirement holds the Context skill.

useCases.name: Look up applicable laws and policies (Legal/Policy Lookup)
useCases.goal: Get candidate standards proposed for a government act, then adopt the right ones.
useCases.trigger: A question needs its legal frame.
useCases.outcome: Labelled proposals kept apart from standards until a member adopts.
useCases.src: Functional Architecture Layer 2 skills; standards Purpose
useCases.coverageNote: The proposal store is required; the lookup skill that produces proposals is not a module.

useCases.name: Discover other groups' published work and 'working on' signals
useCases.goal: Find related work in the network directory; signal what the group is working on.
useCases.outcome: Directory entries and signals.
useCases.src: Design Requirement 10; Roadmap section 11 (Inter-group awareness); Publication section 9 (directory not built)

useCases.name: Record a lead
useCases.goal: Write down what the member knows before searching, so looking has somewhere to start.
useCases.trigger: A member knows or suspects where something is.
useCases.outcome: A private lead readable by its author; never evidence.

useCases.name: Share a lead with a project and record looks at it
useCases.goal: Let a project work a lead and record each look's outcome.
useCases.trigger: A lead bears on a project.
useCases.outcome: Looks in order, with member-facing words for each state.

useCases.name: Read the frontier: what was looked for and what nobody looked at
useCases.goal: Tell which absence is true: nobody looked, looked and found nothing, could not tell, partial, present.
useCases.trigger: Before claiming something is missing, or before preparing a case's searched section.
acts: observation: Read the frontier (what was looked for, what nobody looked at)
useCases.outcome: Four levels (internet, documents, content, meaning) with look states and missing causes.
useCases.src: OBSERVATION-LOG-DESIGN sections 5-6; DEC-86 ('nobody looked' has its own treatment, distinct from Undetermined)

useCases.name: Capture a public document from its address
useCases.goal: Bring a document into the record with provenance: bytes hashed as they arrive, a receipt, a profile.
useCases.trigger: A member finds a document worth keeping.
acts: document: Capture from a public address
useCases.outcome: A collected document with its provenance chain and an earned capture grade (at most B for a direct fetch).
useCases.requirementIds: capture R2, R7-R18, R33-R36; provenance R24

useCases.name: Capture a page as a visitor saw it, from a web archive, or from a Drive link
useCases.goal: Capture sources that do not yield to a simple download.
useCases.trigger: A page renders in the browser, is gone, or lives on Drive.
acts: document: Capture from a public address
useCases.outcome: A rendered pair, an archive capture (grade C at most) or a Drive export, each saying what it is.
useCases.requirementIds: capture R3-R6, R41; capture-sources R1-R46; provenance R25

useCases.name: Supply a source login so a refused capture can succeed
useCases.goal: Unblock a capture that needs credentials, without the secret ever being shown back.
useCases.trigger: A capture request was refused for access.
useCases.outcome: The request retried under a scoped, encrypted, withdrawable credential.

useCases.name: Hand the group material through the doorbell (knock)
useCases.goal: Give material without an account.
useCases.trigger: Someone outside wants the group to have a document.
useCases.outcome: A receipt (knock id, digest, bytes, time); an inbox row; nothing in the record.
useCases.src: Intake Doctrine section 2a; DEC-78 (a knock has a source: an unnamed knocker identified by its receipt)
useCases.coverageNote: Adds the optional knocker secret (at least 20 characters, or one the doorbell makes and shows once) and the pseudonym in the answer.

useCases.name: Move a knock into the record, or discard it
useCases.goal: Read doorbell material and decide whether it becomes part of the record.
useCases.trigger: The doorbell inbox holds new knocks.
acts: knock: Pull: admit the material as a capture
useCases.outcome: Pulled material admitted as a capture at 'collected' carrying the knock's receipt (decided); a discarded knock can be put back to new.
useCases.requirementIds: capture R32, R65, R67, R70, R72; control-plane R36; provenance R19, R42, R51
useCases.src: Intake Doctrine section 2a; DEC-78 (pulling admits the knock's material as a capture carrying its receipt; vouching stays with release)
useCases.coverageNote: Built at the plane; the setup page's 'Mark as taken up' performs the pull (not app.html).

useCases.name: Record a firsthand observation (testimony)
useCases.goal: Put what the member saw or heard into the record in their own words.
useCases.outcome: A collected information bundle graded on the testimony axis, never a capture letter.

useCases.name: Read a document's extracted text and ask for a re-read
useCases.goal: See what the machine read, labelled as machine-read, and ask for OCR when text is missing.
useCases.trigger: Text is absent, partial or undetermined.
useCases.outcome: A reading with its content-axis state (indexed full, partial, none, not extracted, undetermined).
useCases.src: Functional Architecture Function 2; DEC-4 (machine-read text never presented as publisher text)

useCases.name: Point at the part of a document that matters (passage)
useCases.goal: Make a part of a document citable.
useCases.trigger: Only part of a document bears on a question.
useCases.outcome: A content row with its mint label (member-marked or machine work).

useCases.name: Type a transcription of a part; have a second member attest it
useCases.goal: Make an unreadable part citable as text, checked by someone else.
useCases.trigger: Machine text is missing or wrong.
acts: passage: Type a transcription of a part
useCases.outcome: A typed row; the typist cannot attest their own.

useCases.name: Register subjects and declare their relations
useCases.goal: Name the offices, funds, programs and people-in-role a case is about, with aliases and cited relations.
useCases.trigger: A new subject appears in the material.
acts: entity: Declare a relation, with justification and citation
useCases.outcome: Registry entries with no adversarial attribute.

useCases.name: Resolve a document's references to subjects
useCases.goal: Tie what a document names to registered subjects, graded by how the match was made.
useCases.trigger: A document has been captured and read.
acts: entity: Resolve a document's references to subjects
entity: Testify a match the recogniser missed (grade D)
useCases.outcome: Graded matches (A-C by recogniser, D only by member testimony); connections derived.

useCases.name: Declare where a document came from and whether its route can be shown
useCases.goal: Record the office or system a document came from, and assess its route.
acts: document: Declare which office/system it came from
document: Mark whether its route can be shown
useCases.outcome: An attributed declaration; undetermined stays stated.

useCases.name: Release (vouch for) a captured document
useCases.goal: Stand behind a capture after reviewing the source material itself, singly or in bulk with an acknowledgement.
useCases.outcome: The document moves collected to verified with a signed release.
useCases.src: UI-KICKOFF 'Who this is for' item 2; Interaction Constructs section J; DEC-87 (friction follows the rung)
useCases.coverageNote: No approved module owns release's Provides (inventory; inFlux).

useCases.name: Retire a document
useCases.goal: Take a document out of use without erasing it.
useCases.trigger: A document is wrong or superseded.
useCases.outcome: A terminal state; refused while a live edge cites it.
useCases.coverageNote: No approved module owns retire's Provides (inFlux).

useCases.name: Get a trusted timestamp or co-attest a capture
useCases.goal: Add third-party evidence of when bytes existed.
useCases.outcome: An attestation recorded; it never reaches Grade A.
useCases.src: DEC-39; Interaction Constructs section A; DEC-81 (a co-attested Grade B is enough to publish, disclosed on the case)

useCases.name: Declare an expected flow and thread documents into it
useCases.goal: Model how a body is supposed to act (e.g. minutes follow a meeting) and place the documents that show what happened.
useCases.trigger: A recurring process is under watch.
acts: progression: Declare or revise a flow
progression: Thread documents into an instance
useCases.outcome: Declared flow versus observed flow.

useCases.name: Declare themes and place material in them
useCases.goal: Organise material under a named theme with a test; the machine may propose placements.
acts: connection: Declare a theme with its test
connection: Place / propose / withdraw material in a theme
useCases.outcome: Themes that are never evidence.

useCases.name: Assert a connection or choose the on-point mention
useCases.goal: State that two documents are connected, or pick which mention is on point.
useCases.outcome: An attributed choice or assertion with a basis.

useCases.name: Classify material as fact, analysis or judgment
useCases.goal: Keep facts, analysis and judgment separate so each is treated correctly.
useCases.outcome: A classification that travels with the data.
useCases.src: Functional Architecture Layer 2 Function 3; Design Requirement 6 (content classification in metadata)
useCases.coverageNote: No module requirement names the fact / analysis / judgment classification.

useCases.name: Prove later what a public body published
useCases.goal: Keep bytes as served, hashed at receipt, so the record can prove what was available and when.
useCases.outcome: Content-addressed evidence and receipts.
useCases.requirementIds: capture R9, R34; provenance R1-R16, R35
useCases.src: Functional Architecture Function 3; System Design section 1

useCases.name: See the versions the record holds of one address
useCases.goal: Compare versions when a source changed; both are preserved.
useCases.outcome: A version chain with predecessors.

useCases.name: Export the working corpus verifiably
useCases.goal: Move hosts, split or dissolve without losing the record.
acts: case: Export the working corpus verifiably
useCases.outcome: A logged export; every administrator told (queue finding export-performed).
useCases.requirementIds: publication R18-R19, R32; queue R2; queue-producers R2 (export-performed)
useCases.coverageNote: The export-performed producer is queue-producers R2.

useCases.name: Ask for a document to be monitored
useCases.goal: Watch a source at its own cadence (hourly to monthly, per meeting).
useCases.outcome: The document is on the daemon's plan.

useCases.name: Check a source now
useCases.goal: Force a check and see what changed.
useCases.outcome: A look recorded; modified, removed, unchanged or undetermined stated with why.

useCases.name: Be told a source was modified or removed
useCases.goal: Notice changes and removals (possible evidence of concealment), with both versions kept.
useCases.trigger: A monitoring tick flags a change.
useCases.outcome: Queue findings source-modified / source-removed homed under what rests on the document.
useCases.coverageNote: Built; monitoring R31's 'not yet met' mark is stale, since the producers are queue-producers'.

useCases.name: See every watched address, including unscheduled ones
useCases.goal: Know what is and is not being watched.
acts: monitoring: See every watched address, incl. unscheduled
useCases.outcome: A list of addresses with plan rows.

useCases.name: Keep named requests and ratified sweeps running
useCases.goal: Standing intent: fetch what a request or sweep names, on its cadence, within budget.
useCases.outcome: Captures at collected with anomaly notes.

useCases.name: Pause the daemon and read its due slate
useCases.goal: Stop fetching and see what would run; the manual path keeps tools optional.
useCases.outcome: A paused daemon that says so.
useCases.requirementIds: monitoring R30 (built T11-T13: the pause, N314 for every administrator, N324)
useCases.src: Functional Architecture annotation v3; Design Requirement 12 (optional)

useCases.name: Watch the sources a finding rests on
useCases.goal: Have the sources behind an objective or published finding proposed for monitoring.
useCases.trigger: A finding is live or published.
acts: monitoring: Adopt a proposal to watch a finding's sources
useCases.outcome: A proposal to the owning members; never enabled by the machine.

useCases.name: Be told a newer version affects a passage I cited, then adopt or keep
useCases.goal: Update a pinned reference to a newer capture, or keep the earlier one on purpose.
useCases.trigger: A newer capture of a cited address is graded affected or undetermined.
acts: passage: Ask if a newer version holds it
useCases.outcome: A new version of the reference, or a recorded keep.
useCases.requirementIds: reevaluation R14-R15; content R29-R31; queue R1, R12; queue-producers R2
useCases.coverageNote: The producer is queue-producers R2.

useCases.name: Re-evaluate findings when what they rest on changes
useCases.goal: See which findings are affected by supersession, reopening, dismissal or a later edition, and record a re-evaluation.
useCases.trigger: Something a finding rests on moved.
useCases.outcome: Obligations derived on read; a member's recorded re-evaluation closes a cause.
useCases.requirementIds: reevaluation R1-R16, R19-R21 (R17 'weakened' not yet met)
useCases.src: State Rules section 5.4; Functional Architecture Function 4 resolution note

useCases.name: Work the daily queue, grouped by case
useCases.goal: See things that want me: obligations, then queue findings, then conditions, grouped by the case they belong to.
useCases.outcome: One standing entry per case; each item's options pre-flighted for this caller.
useCases.requirementIds: queue R6-R17, R1, R5, R12; queue-producers R15-R18
useCases.src: Interaction Constructs revision 0.2 (QUEUE; DEC-10, DEC-16, DEC-36); queue R1; queue-producers R15-R18
useCases.coverageNote: The four Action kinds are specified in T18, not built.

useCases.name: Resolve or forward obligations, singly or as a set
useCases.goal: Dispatch work addressed to me, or hand it to the right person.
useCases.trigger: An obligation sits in the queue.
acts: queue-item: Resolve / forward an obligation (set form)
useCases.outcome: Resolved for everyone, attributed; per-item answers for a set.
useCases.coverageNote: The tasks module holds obligations; TASK_NOT_YOURS (C-76.1) refuses anyone but the task's actor.

useCases.name: Defer or dismiss a queue finding for my project, with a reason
useCases.goal: Judge something the record noticed, on behalf of one project.
useCases.trigger: A queue finding is homed under my project.
acts: queue-item: Defer / dismiss a finding (set form)
useCases.outcome: The finding leaves that project's list with the reason recorded; other projects unaffected.
useCases.requirementIds: queue R13, R16, R27-R29 (R29 built T12)
useCases.src: Interaction Constructs section P (PROPOSAL); D-79, D-82

useCases.name: Mute, snooze and unmute
useCases.goal: Quiet my own feed without changing the record.
useCases.trigger: Too much noise from one case or item.
acts: queue-item: Mute an item or a case's kinds
useCases.outcome: A personal suppression the feed states; a new kind on a muted case surfaces again.
useCases.requirementIds: queue R4, R14, R19-R22, R40 (R40 built T12)

useCases.name: See who resolved something I did not
useCases.goal: Know that an item left my list because someone else resolved it, not because it vanished.
useCases.trigger: Another member resolved a shared item.
useCases.outcome: 'Resolved by X on this date'.
useCases.requirementIds: queue R39; bias R44; tasks R6
useCases.coverageNote: Built, bias debts included.

useCases.name: Take up a lead into a question or set it aside
useCases.goal: Act on an out-of-inquiry lead at the question's grain.
useCases.trigger: A run captured material bearing on another question.
acts: lead: Take it up into a question / set it aside
useCases.outcome: Cited into the question or set aside with a reason.
useCases.coverageNote: Both halves are marked 'not yet met' (K533) although the queue offers the acts: unproven.

useCases.name: Decide an obligation the record routed to me (authority, endorsement, expertise, ratification request)
useCases.goal: Answer a task: determine authority on an undetermined capture, endorse, confirm expertise, answer a join request.
useCases.trigger: A task is routed to me (owner, else first citing project's owner, else earliest administrator, else unassigned).
acts: queue-item: Act on the subject directly
useCases.outcome: The act runs in its own surface; the task resolves.
useCases.requirementIds: queue R1, R8, R12; tasks R1-R3

useCases.name: Open a question
useCases.goal: Start an inquiry on what the member wants to know; the assistant may surface one within a run's bound.
useCases.outcome: An open (or surfaced, marked) question.
useCases.requirementIds: inquiry R1-R2; ai-runs R25-R27; intent R16

useCases.name: Cite material into a question, supporting or cutting against
useCases.goal: Say 'this is why I think that', with legs whose grades are earned, not asserted.
useCases.outcome: Legs with earned grades; ungraded legs inert and named.
useCases.requirementIds: citation R1-R3, R7-R8; inquiry R4-R8, R13-R14, R32, R34
useCases.src: Case Making; invariant 7 (what cuts against travels the same path)

useCases.name: Sever or reinstate a citation on a case
useCases.goal: Withdraw or restore a project's citation, with a reason.
acts: leg: Sever / reinstate on a case
useCases.outcome: An edge marked severed, never erased.

useCases.name: Narrow a leg to the on-point part
useCases.goal: Cite only the part that matters; the machine may propose candidates.
acts: leg: Narrow to the on-point part
useCases.outcome: A new suggested version derived from the old.

useCases.name: Group legs into independent grounds
useCases.goal: Say that separate bodies of support each suffice, by an attributed act.
useCases.trigger: A question has several lines of support.
acts: inquiry: Group the legs into sets of reasons
useCases.outcome: Grounds recorded with who asserted them; strength before and after shown after structure is authored.
useCases.requirementIds: inquiry R8, R27-R28; strength R4, R17; affordances R5

useCases.name: Check whether grounds share an origin
useCases.goal: Make sure 'independent' grounds do not trace to one source.
acts: strength: Check whether sets of reasons share an origin
useCases.outcome: An independence answer per pair of parts.

useCases.name: Read how strong a question or version is
useCases.goal: See the pair (weakest capture, weakest connection) with testimony beside it, and what is not load-bearing.
useCases.trigger: Before concluding or preparing a case.
acts: strength: Read strength of a question or version
useCases.outcome: Per-axis grades; unrated and undetermined stated; what-ifs labelled.
useCases.src: DEC-21, DEC-44; Case Making R1-R2; DEC-82 (the workspace shows the strength pair against the bar; measures map); DEC-86 (Undetermined and 'unrated' each have their own treatment)

useCases.name: Compare alternative accounts of support and decide on them
useCases.goal: Accept, reject, consider or revert basis versions (including machine-suggested ones), previewing first.
useCases.trigger: A question has more than one version.
useCases.outcome: Member-authored version states; the machine never accepts.

useCases.name: Make a version current for my project
useCases.goal: Choose which accepted account the project stands on.
acts: basis-version: Make current for a project
useCases.outcome: The project's CURRENT; other projects unaffected.

useCases.name: Conclude a question, stating what would falsify it
useCases.goal: Adopt the current version's claim for the project, with a falsifier or a stated 'none'.
useCases.trigger: The member judges the support sufficient.
useCases.outcome: A dated, authored conclusion row: a concluded finding for this project.
useCases.src: DEC-24 (the member does the concluding); Case Making; DEC-82 (strength shown against the bar where a question is concluded)

useCases.name: Withdraw a project's conclusion
useCases.goal: Take back a conclusion with a reason; history stays.
useCases.outcome: An appended withdrawal row.

useCases.name: Reopen a finding
useCases.goal: Return a concluded or set-down question to work; a published case member's only route to change.
useCases.outcome: A reopened question saying who reopened it.

useCases.name: Divide a question into sub-questions
useCases.goal: Split a question, apportioning every leg including those that cut against.
useCases.outcome: A divided parent and children, landing together.

useCases.name: Set a question aside (defer or dismiss) with a reason
useCases.goal: Park or drop a question without deleting it.
useCases.trigger: A question is not worth pursuing now.
useCases.outcome: A recorded disposition; one team's disposition never moves another's stance.

useCases.name: Follow a hunch, then clear it before publishing
useCases.goal: Temporarily connect evidence ahead of support; the hunch must be cleared before publication.
useCases.trigger: Nothing else joins the evidence up.
acts: bias-debt: Clear a hunch before publishing
useCases.outcome: Hunch legs inert in strength; publication refused UNCLEARED_HUNCH.
useCases.coverageNote: Publishing refuses an uncleared hunch; a hunch still counts at its stated grade in strength (R5 not yet met).

useCases.name: Declare a standard from its captured text
useCases.goal: Hold what a government act is measured against, by citation and its own words as captured.
useCases.trigger: A law, policy or commitment applies.
useCases.outcome: A standard with declarer and time; never edited.

useCases.name: Ask what standard was in force on a date
useCases.goal: Know whether a standard applied when the act happened.
acts: standard: Ask what was in force on a date
useCases.outcome: in_force / not_in_force / undetermined, with why.

useCases.name: Compare a government act to its standards (Government Compliance Analysis)
useCases.goal: Get a structured comparison: what the standard requires, what the body did, where they align and diverge, what is still unknown.

acts: determination: Read the facts for a comparison from a contradiction
useCases.outcome: A labelled proposal for human evaluation, never a determination.

useCases.name: Turn an unclear outcome into questions
useCases.goal: Return to Layer 1 when information is insufficient.
acts: determination: Open a question from an unclear outcome
useCases.outcome: Named questions opened or linked.

useCases.name: Judge significance: is this worth escalating?

escalation: Advance / decline a proposed stage
escalation: Open from a live noncompliant determination

useCases.goal: State the standard of evidence the project's productions are held to.

useCases.goal: Make the group's lens part of the record: scrutiny, inference and pattern statements, each justified.
useCases.trigger: A group knows its standing positions.
useCases.outcome: A lens in force; malformed verdict statements refused.

journeyExperience.journey: (a) A group sets up and invites members
journeyExperience.spans: days; several people (operator, founder, second administrator, members)

steps.step: Install the signed release into the group's account
steps.whatTheyKnow: Needs a paid account with a payment method; the page states prerequisites.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Which slug to use (written once, public forever) and which jurisdiction profiles to offer.
whatCanGoWrong: Existing copy for the slug: refused, nothing changed (installer R5).
No payment method: refused, saying nothing was created (installer R4, R7).
Account already holds a copy: refused until installs are isolated (installer R32).
A part not serving the release: named, not claimed as done (installer R15, R33).
steps.howLong: One sitting; up to ten self-test tries.
steps.feelingRisk: The slug is public and permanent; a group wanting anonymity must choose an unrevealing one now.
steps.src: installer R2-R16, R21-R24, R32-R33; Publication section 7 point 1
openInThisStep: How the operator is told, in plain words, that the slug is permanent and public at the moment of choosing.

steps.step: Open the setup page and claim with the one-time password
steps.whatTheyKnow: Holds the password (the link may carry it as #boot=).
steps.decisionTheyMake: Choose a password of at least 12 characters.
whatCanGoWrong: ALREADY_CLAIMED (membership R1).
PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT.
The page could not read the group: says so, never 'none recorded' (instance-setup R20).
steps.feelingRisk: The founder becomes the root of trust with no custody model (DEC-2 deferred).
steps.src: membership R1; instance-setup R20-R22; control-plane R15

steps.step: Set display name, domain and jurisdiction profiles
steps.whatTheyKnow: The slug; the held profiles by name and coverage.
steps.decisionTheyMake: What the group calls itself; which domain to claim; which profiles (none preselected).
whatCanGoWrong: GROUP_DISPLAY_NAME_MALFORMED.
Domain verdict absent, mismatched or UNDETERMINED: not shown publicly; members see the state (instance-setup R8-R10).
Changing profiles changes how local facts read (warning; instance-setup R15).
steps.feelingRisk: Showing an unverified domain would claim an association the record cannot support.
steps.src: instance-setup R5-R16; Publication section 7 (profiles built T12, N10)

steps.step: Add a second administrator (direct while fewer than two)
steps.whatTheyKnow: The floor is two administrators.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Who, with what cover (not a legal name).
whatCanGoWrong: NOT_AN_ADMIN.
Cover typed as a legal name defeats the protection (Membership v2 section 3).
steps.howLong: Minutes; then waits for the invitee.
steps.feelingRisk: Cover invites a legal name if the field is worded badly.

steps.step: Record who holds hosting access
steps.whoIsActing: the group, asked when the second administrator is added
steps.whatTheyKnow: Hosting access is outside the app.
whatCanGoWrong: Left unanswered: the record keeps whatever answer was given.
steps.feelingRisk: None named in canon.
openInThisStep: What the group is told about why this matters (the hosting account is the remedy against the founder).

steps.step: Add members with capabilities (default contribute)
steps.whatTheyKnow: Capabilities: contribute, publish, create_projects.
whatCanGoWrong: At two or more administrators, a new administrator is only proposed and needs a ballot (membership R14).
BAD_CAPABILITY.
steps.handoffTo: invitee (burner URL sent by a channel the system does not record)
steps.feelingRisk: None named.
steps.src: membership R9, R12-R15; Membership v2 section 6

steps.step: Open the link, choose handle and password
steps.whatTheyKnow: Sees cover, role, capabilities and expertise; never the member id.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Handle (public in the record) and password.
whatCanGoWrong: NO_SUCH_INVITATION (spent or never existed, one answer).
HANDLE_TAKEN.
BAD_HANDLE.
PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT.
steps.howLong: Minutes; the link is spent on use.
steps.feelingRisk: The handle is what the public sees; the member may not realise.
openInThisStep: What a newcomer learns first is deferred until the redesign is built and stable (DEC-91); meanwhile strength against the bar and 'Undetermined' come first (DEC-82).

steps.step: Create a project with an objective
steps.whatTheyKnow: A project name is unique across the instance.
whatCanGoWrong: NAME_TAKEN.
A project with no objective is refused (intent R1).
steps.feelingRisk: Members may believe projects are private; visibility is organisation, not secrecy.
steps.src: promotion R19; intent R1; membership R71; Membership v2 section 2

steps.step: Invite participants; they join
steps.whatTheyKnow: Handles.
whatCanGoWrong: NOT_THE_OWNER.
NO_SUCH_HANDLE.
ALREADY_A_PARTICIPANT.
NOT_INVITED on join.
steps.feelingRisk: None named.

steps.step: Make the project discoverable; an outsider requests to join; owner grants
steps.whatTheyKnow: Outsiders see the name only.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Whether to expose the name; whether to grant.
whatCanGoWrong: PROJECT_SEEN_NOT_A_PARTICIPANT (C-70.1) for acts beyond existence.
A grant invites; the requester still has to join (membership R51).
steps.feelingRisk: Exposing a name tells every member the project exists.

journeyExperience.journey: (b) From a question to a published case
journeyExperience.spans: weeks; several members, possibly an outside reviewer

steps.step: Capture a public document
steps.whatTheyKnow: An address.
whatCanGoWrong: BAD_LOCATOR.
HOST_COOLING_OFF: the governor paces the host (capture R7).
Source refused or fetch failed, recorded as such (capture R8).
Rendered content UNDETERMINED; archive capture at most C.
steps.howLong: Seconds to minutes; renders may be deferred.
steps.feelingRisk: A capture is not evidence until a member stands behind it; the grade note may be discarded before the member sees it (DEC-51).
steps.src: capture R2-R18; AI Roles rule 4; DEC-51

steps.step: Release it (vouch for it)
steps.whatTheyKnow: Must see the source material itself, never only an AI summary.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Stand behind it, with acknowledgement and mitigation for a bulk release.
whatCanGoWrong: Refused with offenders named (weight refuse: all or nothing).
A second member released first: CAS_STALE (promotion R1).
steps.feelingRisk: Click-through bulk release would make the acknowledgement dishonest.
steps.src: UI-KICKOFF item 2; Interaction Constructs section J; affordances R1-R2
openInThisStep: No owning module requirement holds release (inFlux).

steps.step: Resolve its references to subjects
steps.whatTheyKnow: Recognised references with grades.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Accept matches; testify a missed one (grade D).
whatCanGoWrong: Ambiguous alias kept, never resolved silently (entities R6).
A C match never reads established.
steps.feelingRisk: One click from an established resolution off a machine-composed list (DEC-53).

steps.step: Open a question (or the assistant surfaces one)
steps.whatTheyKnow: What they want to know.
whatCanGoWrong: Surfaced by the assistant: must look surfaced; ages to deferred if nobody acts (intent R17).
steps.howLong: Minutes; ageing interval set per instance.
steps.feelingRisk: A machine question must not read as a member's obligation (D-82).
steps.src: inquiry R1-R2; ai-runs R25-R27; intent R16-R17

steps.step: Cite documents, passages or questions as supporting or cutting against
steps.whatTheyKnow: Earned grades per target.
whatCanGoWrong: RETIRED_NOT_CITABLE.
A grouped question refuses a new leg until ungrouped (DEC-50).
A newer capture may exist: stale version notice.
A supporting and a cutting-against leg that conflict carry a tension mark; the clarifier asks how they differ (decided: DEC-77).
steps.feelingRisk: Stating a grade the record did not earn: the leg is capped and why is shown.

steps.step: Open an assistant run to check or investigate
steps.whatTheyKnow: The run's bounds, lens and bar are recorded at open.
whatCanGoWrong: Mode not deployed: refused (ai-runs R40).
A bound stops the run and the log says which.
Capture requests wait on the daemon (hours).
steps.feelingRisk: The assistant appearing to conclude; transcripts are notes, never record.
steps.src: ai-runs R9-R24, R40; AI Roles section 3

steps.step: Accept a version (after the shared-origin check)
steps.whatTheyKnow: Versions with legs and per-axis strength; suggested ones labelled.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Accept, reject, consider, revert; preview first.
whatCanGoWrong: VERSION_* refusals; MACHINE_CANNOT_MOVE_VERSION for a machine.
Grounds that share an origin.
steps.feelingRisk: Accepting a machine suggestion without reading it (DEC-68: the record cannot tell).

steps.step: Make it current for the project
steps.whatTheyKnow: Which version is accepted.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Which account the project stands on.
whatCanGoWrong: VERSION_NOT_ACCEPTED.
Not a joined participant.
steps.feelingRisk: None named.

steps.step: Conclude, stating what would falsify it (or that nothing would)
steps.whatTheyKnow: The current version and its strength.
whatCanGoWrong: MACHINE_CANNOT_CONCLUDE.
NO_CLAIM.
Another project concluded differently: both stances stand.
steps.feelingRisk: False certainty: a falsifier of 'none' must be the member's stated override.

steps.step: Check strength against the bar; clear hunches
steps.whatTheyKnow: Per-axis pair per load-bearing finding; the project bar.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Which findings are load-bearing; which hunches to clear.
whatCanGoWrong: BELOW_PROJECT_STRENGTH naming member, axis, required and reached (case-authoring R6).
UNCLEARED_HUNCH (not yet enforced; lands with the ceremony's pre-flight, DEC-80 item 3).
steps.howLong: Days if more evidence is needed.
steps.feelingRisk: Over-claiming: a case over an uncleared hunch states a strength that is not true.
steps.src: case-authoring R6, R12; strength R5; DEC-20

steps.step: Draft a review copy; grant outside reviewers
steps.whatTheyKnow: The copy is complete as a publication can be and names what is missing.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Whom to grant; when to revoke.
whatCanGoWrong: Grant dies if the draft moves case identity (review R8).
Recipient sees findings as the last editor could, absent ones by role only.
steps.feelingRisk: Calling it 'pre-publish' asserts a future that may not happen.

steps.step: Prepare the case: scope, statement, exclusions, bias acknowledgement
steps.whatTheyKnow: Concluded findings; the searched section computed from the log.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Roles, scope, what is left out and why.
whatCanGoWrong: COMPLETENESS_CARRIED_FORWARD (byte-identical to last edition).
CASE_SEARCHED_UNCOMPUTABLE.
ALREADY_A_CASE_MEMBER.
CASE_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS.
steps.feelingRisk: Nothing may draft framing for the member (Case Making section 4a).

steps.step: Acknowledge the exclusion statement
steps.whoIsActing: joined participant or review recipient (not its writer)
steps.whatTheyKnow: The statement, shown first.
whatCanGoWrong: STATEMENT_ACK_BY_ITS_AUTHOR.
STATEMENT_ACK_NOT_A_PARTICIPANT.
STATEMENT_ACK_ALREADY_SIGNED.
STATEMENT_ACK_AUTHOR_UNDETERMINED.
steps.feelingRisk: A gate pushing a one-person group to recruit a signature would be a bug; nobody-but-author is disclosed, not refused.

steps.step: Go through the publication ceremony and sign in the browser
steps.whatTheyKnow: Before the first screen, what would stop publication (the pre-flight). Then: what becomes permanent; what it rests on; what it leaves out, including any unresolved record contradiction to disclose and consent for any source identity it would reveal; the edition it creates (DEC-80 item 2).
steps.decisionTheyMake: Disclose, acknowledge, and sign now or not.
whatCanGoWrong: NO_SIGNERS.
CASE_RATIFY_STALE (an acknowledgement or edit re-authored it).
ATTRIBUTION_UNCHOSEN / ATTRIBUTION_STATEMENT_STALE.
OPERATOR_TOKEN_CANNOT_RATIFY_CASE.
CASE_CONCLUSION_MOVED.
An undisclosed open record tension refuses the case; a disclosed one does not (DEC-84 (13)).
A load-bearing document whose co-attestation failed: retried, then acknowledged with a reason and marked 'self-attested only' (DEC-81 item 3).
A finding rests on a side in conflict with a record the owner cannot see: told in the ceremony, highlighted in the case, never naming that record (DEC-85).
steps.howLong: Minutes, once the pre-flight is clear.
steps.feelingRisk: A member who thinks they certify authenticity has been misled (Interaction Constructs section A).
steps.src: ratification R2-R3; DEC-80; DEC-81; DEC-76 item 4; DEC-78 item 5; case-authoring R31-R37; ratification R18-R19
openInThisStep: Built at the plane (the pre-flight, the tensions read, the late retry, capture accounts, self-registered keys); the five screens and signing in the browser are not built; the words of each step are the redesign's.

steps.step: Ratify each finding and its evidence
steps.whatTheyKnow: Pinned members awaiting signature.
whatCanGoWrong: RATIFY_FINDING_NOT_IN_A_RATIFIED_CASE.
RATIFY_NOT_EVIDENCE_OF_A_RATIFIED_CASE.
A finding ratified before its evidence does not link to it on the published graph (Publication section 3 rule 2 gap).
steps.feelingRisk: Irreversible: correction only by a new edition.

steps.step: Read and verify by hash
steps.whatTheyKnow: No account.
whatCanGoWrong: Not published: stated.
A finding pinned by several cases: the reader chooses (FINDING_IN_SEVERAL_CASES).
Cases disagree on a finding's pair: CASES_DISAGREE, each case's pair shown.
steps.feelingRisk: Reading strength as a single score, or authenticity into a hash.

journeyExperience.spans: weeks to months; statutory clocks; several members; outside offices and counsel

steps.step: Declare the standard (or adopt a proposal)
steps.whatTheyKnow: The standard's captured text; profile source match.
whatCanGoWrong: MACHINE_CANNOT_DECLARE_STANDARD.
STANDARD_NO_CITE.
Source undetermined when the profile does not supply it.
steps.feelingRisk: None named.

steps.step: Record a determination per standard
steps.whatTheyKnow: Published findings with frozen pairs; standards in force.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Compliant, noncompliant or unclear, per standard.
whatCanGoWrong: A standard not in force at the act's date: refused.
Any significance, rank or score key: refused (R8).
basis_changed later when a finding reopens.
steps.feelingRisk: Judging significance through policy preference (Functional Architecture Function 4).

steps.step: Record consequences
steps.whatTheyKnow: What the record can compute; what must be assessed.
whatCanGoWrong: NOT_NONCOMPLIANT.
A part naming an individual: refused.
Totals only within one state.
steps.feelingRisk: Composing harm into one headline figure (refused).

steps.step: Open an escalation
steps.whatTheyKnow: The determination is live and noncompliant.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Whether to pursue, and why, in their own words (decided: DEC-89).
whatCanGoWrong: MACHINE_CANNOT_OPEN.
DETERMINATION_SUPERSEDED.
steps.feelingRisk: None named.

steps.step: Or decline to escalate, saying why not now
steps.whatTheyKnow: The determination is live and noncompliant.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Why the group is not pursuing it now, in their own words.
whatCanGoWrong: Nothing may be recorded as significance, severity, priority, urgency or rank (conformance R8, escalation R19).
steps.handoffTo: the group; a later escalation, opened with its own reason, supersedes it and both stay readable
steps.feelingRisk: Until it is built, deciding not to escalate leaves no trace.
openInThisStep: Decided, not built: escalation, conformance and affordances requirements owed.

steps.step: Create a breach action to the office; set the risk tier
steps.whatTheyKnow: Counterparty by role and body from the profile.
steps.decisionTheyMake: Tier 1, 2 or 3 with a reason; governing laws.
whatCanGoWrong: Tier unset reads UNDETERMINED, never 1 (D-182).
MACHINE_CANNOT_SET_RISK_TIER.
LEASE_HELD (another member acting on the action).
steps.feelingRisk: Legally unsophisticated filing creating adverse precedent (Tier 3).

steps.step: Prepare, approve and record the filing sent
steps.whatTheyKnow: Draft with [UNFILLED] blanks; Tier 2 advisory first.

purpose.text: Things that want me, grouped by the case they belong to; the one way work reaches a person.

mustShow.text: Class of each item: obligation (do / forward / resolve), queue finding (adopt / defer / dismiss), condition (status or mute).
A queue finding must look derived: its source and derivation, and that nobody has judged it yet.
Agent-surfaced marker wherever a question appears.
Resolved by X on this date, for items someone else resolved.
What my mutes and snoozes are suppressing, with an undo.
mustShow.src: queue R14, R40; System Design row 12 (UI-97)

mustShow.text: Each option's rung and set weight, pre-flighted for this caller.
An obligation's own resolving act, as the item publishes it.
The finding class labelled 'Noticed'.
A record contradiction as a duty that cannot be muted or dismissed, leaving only by resolution; a world one as a lead dismissed in one act with a fixed reason.
A newer capture that affects a member's reference, with adopt and keep.
Each obligation's 'instead' names its own door: signerset for a self-registered key, biasdebtresolve for a bias debt, taskresolve otherwise.
A conflict with a record the member cannot see, homed only from the member's own side (contradiction-duty-unseen, contradiction-plurality-unseen).
Whose it is: the group's own (a checkpoint, marked 'ours') or the counterparty's (a deadline: 'the counterparty's deadline, not ours').
mustShow.src: PATH.md §3; build/plan/action-design/surfaces.html (design view, not stated as approved)

mustShow.text: A checkpoint due: the plan, scenario and phase, and its condition; judged met or not met with a note.
A proposed stage: 'a member advances or declines with a reason; the system never advances'.
mustShow.src: queue-producers R17; build/plan/action-design/surfaces.html (design view, not stated as approved)

mustShow.text: A reminder the member asked for, to that member only; its answer offers another reminder on a later day or none.
mustShow.src: queue-producers R18; action-clocks R6; DEC-10 (D-125); DEC-94 (1)

mustShow.text: An overdue deadline as a CONDITION naming the entry's date, basis and text, raised once.
As a deadline nears, position, colour or wording may change: display, not a notification.

mustNeverShowOrDo.text: Never nag: one standing entry per (member, case); re-notify only on snooze expiry or something new.
Never present a machine finding as an obligation; one check across 58 contracts is one proposal with 58 instances.
Never let a mute look like a record act, or a dismissal look personal.
Never mute an obligation.
Never a severity ladder of warning / error colours in place of the three classes.
Never reveal a task on a subject the viewer may not see: it reads as no task.
A missed or not-met checkpoint as a finding, a condition of the record or a fact about the government.
Repeat anything unless the member asked; 'due within N days' is not new unless requested.
Any outside channel (email, push).

undetermined.text: One component with a fixed mark and a mandatory 'because…' line, the same everywhere; never an error, never a zero.

withheld.text: Something exists the viewer may not see: its own treatment and one fixed sentence stating the incompleteness, never identity, title, state or count.

refused.text: The plane's refusal in its own words with offenders named: the shared sentence first, then the act's own next step or alternative; never 'something went wrong'.

truncated.text: Every list says when it was cut at a stated bound.

empty.text: What does an empty queue say (nothing wants you, versus nothing could be read)?

stale.text: A snoozed case's items are marked snoozed until the instant, not withheld by the plane.

conflict.text: Another member resolved a shared item: show attribution, not a gap.

ungrouped.text: Items with no case sit ungrouped; a home set that is undetermined is stated.

reversible (DEC-88; the code still lists it as undetermined)

accessibilityAndLanguage.text: Phones supported, acceptably as a viewing MVP; features may be absent on some devices.
Plain, reader-language meaning for every state, from one semantics table; every chip is a click-over disclosing its row.
No accessibility standard (screen reader, keyboard, contrast) is named in canon; the UI plan records the hardening pass as absent. What level is required?
No language other than English is named in canon. Must the product or its published output be multilingual?

surfaceRules.surface: ACT (the one motion for doing something to a record or a set)

purpose.text: Choose; see what it will refuse and why before it runs; author the reason; get a receipt.

mustShow.text: Every act's button carries its rung's name and weight pips. Friction follows the rung: reversible inline; reasoned a reason field in place; terminal and attested a full dialog stating what ends or cannot be silently undone, and who signs; irreversible only through the ceremony.
For a set: whether the act is all-or-nothing, report-and-proceed, or per-item, before acting.
The ballot's denominator: '2 of 3', never 'pending approval'; the divergence at two owners shown.
The receipt: what was written, by whom, when; a preview answers with nothing written.

An act whose effect cannot be taken back outside the record opens the full dialog stating that effect, whatever its rung: attributing a name, sharing a lead, naming a person in the registry, setting the group bar.

openQuestions.question: How is a contradiction presented to a member, and what does resolving one look like (both sides in the record's words; a resolution that records its kind and may promote double-speak into a finding)?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Contradictions are 'golden nuggets' the system exists to find; in our own record they carry a duty to resolve. PRESENT and RESOLVE are undesigned and nothing shows a candidate to a member.
openQuestions.context: A contradiction is two things the record holds that cannot both be true. The system already pairs statements worth comparing and lets an AI run label each pair (in the world, in our own record, a difference of precision, unrelated, undetermined), but these 'candidates' are stored out of sight; no member sees them yet.

canonSays.says: Three cases: in the WORLD a finding, 'drawn attention to' and never fixed; in our RECORD a defect with a duty to identify, present and resolve; a difference of precision is no contradiction.
PRESENT: a member sees both sides in the record's own words, never a machine verdict. RESOLVE: a member's attributed act that never deletes either side.
At least one resolution kind must be able to promote the conflict into a finding: double-speak found while cleaning our record becomes a finding about the subject.
Labels are world, record, precision, unrelated, undetermined; a candidate is 'proposed machine work and no finding'; no read shows one to a member.

openQuestions.whyOpen: Only detection is designed and built. Nothing says where a candidate appears, what 'both sides with enough context' contains, which resolution kinds exist (misquote, our capture error, genuine double-speak, difference of opinion), or what promotion to a finding does. The irreconcilable pair (two well-supported findings the group keeps both of) needs a claim object Bob has not ruled on. Detection passed its gate (0/17 false conflicts, M-162) only on a test fixture, not real documents.
openQuestions.todayInOldUI: Nothing: the old interface never shows a contradiction candidate.

options.option: Show candidates as 'Noticed' queue items opening a side-by-side page (side A, side B, each with document, date and surrounding passage), with resolve acts named by kind
options.tradeoffs: Uses the one queue members already learn; could flood it if real false conflicts exceed the fixture's.

options.option: Show them only in place, as a mark on the question or document where a side sits
options.tradeoffs: Quieter and in context; a conflict between two projects' work may never be seen by anyone.

options.option: Design 'record' conflicts first (the duty) and treat 'world' candidates as a prompt to open a question whose conclusion is the discrepancy
options.tradeoffs: Matches the doctrine's priorities and reuses built question acts; the irreconcilable pair still waits for Bob.

openQuestions.recommendation: The third option, delivered through the first (a Noticed item opening a side-by-side page), with a resolution vocabulary Bob approves; measure false conflicts on real documents before anything reaches members.
openQuestions.whoDecides: Bob for the resolution kinds, the promotion to a finding and the irreconcilable pair (doctrine); Design for the side-by-side layout within them.

ruled.decided: A contradiction is conditional: two assertions that cannot both hold in the same respect. Resolving one means finding the respect in which they differ, finding the side that is wrong, or recording that the conflict is genuine. A candidate a member takes up becomes an inquiry whose conclusion records its kind (dissolved, corrected, or genuine; double-speak becomes a finding, and an obligation set against an act goes to conformance). It is shown inline wherever the two points already sit, through a tension mark and a short 'how do these differ' clarifier, with a dedicated contradiction screen only as the escalation; context may fill in facts and recommend judgements, labelled, but never silently decides. An undetermined candidate is a lead, never a duty; a record duty binds the joined members of every project drawing on either side until it is resolved; two projects' different conclusions are plurality unless they cannot both hold in the same respect, when a tension mark asks how they differ; the machine recommends only which respects may differ; a hypothesised cause is published as 'cause not established'; publication discloses, never blocks; 'one of them is wrong' needs a written reason; a dismissal gives one fixed reason. When the other side is in a project a member cannot see, each project is told of the conflict on its own side only; a checkbox signals willingness to resolve it, and when both projects opt in their members respond through relayed notices, sharing only what each chooses; a conflict remaining at publication is highlighted without naming the hidden project (DEC-85).
ruled.title: Contradictions: how they are shown and resolved

openQuestions.question: How does a knock become part of the record: what does 'pulled' commit a member to, and does the capture name the doorbell as its provenance?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: It is the only route in for whistleblowers and outsiders, and unvetted material must never look vouched for.
openQuestions.context: The doorbell lets anyone, with no account, hand the group a file or text (a 'knock'), for example a whistleblower. The knocker gets a receipt; the material sits in a separate doorbell inbox and is not part of the record. A signed-in member reads each knock and marks it 'pulled', 'discarded' or back to 'new'.

canonSays.says: A knock 'does not enter the record by knocking'; the intake contract and the provenance-for-admission rule 'apply when a member brings its material in, not before'.

What comes through the doorbell 'has NO attributed source, and the record says so rather than supplying one'; hand-carried material must be attributed to a member, 'as distinct from anonymous material arriving through the doorbell'.
Every submission carries provenance: a locator (an address, or 'in hand' with chain-of-custody notes), who issued it, when, the capture method and the capturing actor.
Resolving records only the status (pulled, discarded, new), who and when; nothing else changes.

openQuestions.whyOpen: 'Pulled' is only a label today: it creates no capture and nothing links the knock to a later one. Two rules pull apart: the intake contract wants a named locator and issuer, while the doorbell doctrine says the source is unknown and must be stated as unknown. Also undecided: whether pulling vouches for the material (release, a weightier act) or only admits it unvetted, and whether the knocker's note and contact travel into the record.
openQuestions.todayInOldUI: Nothing: the old interface has no doorbell inbox or knock screen.

options.option: 'Pull' creates a capture at 'collected' whose provenance says 'received through the doorbell, source unknown' plus the knock id and digest, and commits the member to nothing more
options.tradeoffs: Honest and simple; release (vouching) stays a separate later act. Needs a doorbell provenance class in the capture module.

options.option: Pulling is itself the member vouching: they become the hand-carrying source
options.tradeoffs: One step, but it turns an anonymous source into a named one, which Membership §1.2 forbids.

options.option: Keep 'pulled' a status only; the member uploads the material separately and writes chain-of-custody notes
options.tradeoffs: No new mechanism, but the link to the knock is manual and can be lost or misstated.

openQuestions.recommendation: The first option: pulling admits the material with 'doorbell, source unknown' as its stated provenance, and vouching stays with release.
openQuestions.whoDecides: Bob: whether pulling vouches and how anonymous provenance is stated are intake doctrine; Design settles the inbox screens afterward.

ruled.decided: Pulling a knock admits its material as a capture at 'collected' carrying the knock's receipt, and commits the member to nothing more; vouching stays with release. The source is recorded as an unnamed knocker identified by the receipt (never 'unknown'), the pulling member is the capturing actor and never the source, a knocker may prove continuity with a secret they keep, and a source's identity is held as a dated history of disclosures, published only with consent. The note travels with the capture as the knocker's own words; the contact stays in the inbox. The inbox act is regraded reasoned once pulling admits material (DEC-88).
ruled.title: A knock: how a tip becomes part of the record

openQuestions.question: Does a project show a stage (forming, investigating, matured, closed) and a work-product readiness ladder, and how?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: The Roadmap's project workspace has phase bars; the lifecycle and readiness ladder exist in canon only and no requirement holds them.
openQuestions.context: A project is a group's line of work around a stated objective. The canon gives it a stage (forming, investigating, matured, closed) and gives its work product a readiness ladder (draft, internally checked, externally compliant, distributed), so members can see where the work stands.

canonSays.says: A project shows its stage, one of State Rules §4.3's four, 'derived and never set by hand', with its work products' readiness, computed from the questions it holds and what it has published; the redesign shows it on the project's home screen (T12).
Lifecycle: forming (scope settling) → investigating → matured (analysis supports a defensible position) → closed, with a closed_reason (resolved, superseded, abandoned), 'preserved, reversible'.

The readiness ladder advances only on recorded evaluations: internally_checked needs passing internal compliance and argument evaluations; externally_compliant passing external ones; distributed at least one distribution record.
The workproduct_state, evaluations and closed_reason checks stay in legacy code; no module requirement holds the lifecycle or ladder.

openQuestions.whyOpen: K356 settles that the stage is shown and derived. Still open: the derivation rule (what moves forming to investigating, or to matured), which BOB must word before T12 (N300). 'Closed' carries a judged reason (resolved, superseded, abandoned), which sits uneasily with 'never set by hand'. The ladder advances on compliance and argument evaluations that are not built (UC-100), and the Roadmap's 'phase bars with tooltips' are undesigned.
openQuestions.todayInOldUI: The workspace shows the readiness ladder read-only from the document's workproduct_state; the lifecycle is a stored state with chips and allows closed back to investigating.

options.option: Derive all four stages: forming until a question has a leg, investigating while questions are open, matured when a question has concluded, closed only by an owner's reasoned act that the display then shows
options.tradeoffs: Clear and mostly automatic; 'closed' remains an authored act, a stated exception to 'never by hand'.

options.option: Derive stage only and drop the readiness ladder until evaluations exist
options.tradeoffs: Avoids showing a ladder that never moves; loses the path-to-publication signal the Roadmap wanted.

options.option: Show both, the ladder with its unmet rungs stated as 'no evaluation recorded'
options.tradeoffs: Honest about absence; a ladder that never moves may read as failure.

openQuestions.recommendation: The first option for stage, with the ladder shown only for rungs the record can actually earn, each unearned rung stated rather than hidden.
openQuestions.whoDecides: Bob confirms whether 'closed' may be an authored act despite K356 (requirement); Design settles the phase-bar layout; BOB words the derivation (N300).

ruled.decided: All four stages are shown: 'forming', 'investigating' and 'matured' are computed from the record, and 'closed' is the owner's reasoned act. Only readiness rungs a case can earn are shown, and each unearned one is stated. The display is coloured bars that build up, one per stage reached, disclosing more on hover (with a focus or tap equivalent) and opening on click to what each stage needs next and when each was reached; each bar is named, and 'closed' shows its reason and never reads as a finished stack.
ruled.title: A project's stage and its cases' readiness

openQuestions.question: What are the five steps of the publication ceremony, and what does the placeholder say until it is built?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Publication is the only irreversible act and the ceremony is the safeguard; its process is deferred (DEC-33).
openQuestions.context: Publishing a case is the one act that cannot be taken back; corrections only move forward as new editions. The 'ceremony' is the deliberate screen sequence an owner goes through before signing. Bob deferred it; today the group's operator publishes and members see a placeholder page.

canonSays.says: 'The publication process is very involved. Defer anything related to the process, though create a placeholder surface.' UI-17 (the five-step ceremony) and REC-15 (its dry run) are deferred.
The ceremony reopens with Program B's member surfaces or the first self-run group, whichever first; until then a member reaches the placeholder and is told, once, what is not yet there (DEC-69).
The pre-flight is plane-sourced: op=publishpreflight runs the real refusals (uncleared hunch, below the project's strength, no signers) without writing, because the browser cannot compute them.
The top rung 'carries its own ceremony (what becomes permanent, what it does and does not claim, an explicit key act)'; 'the ceremony IS the safeguard'.

openQuestions.whyOpen: The five steps are named only in archived research, not in canon: What becomes permanent; What this rests on; What you are leaving out (the gate); The revision this creates; Sign (BUILD-ORDER UI-17, RECONCILED). They predate DEC-72, which made a case a production of a project signed by an owner, so they may need re-deriving. The placeholder's wording is also not fixed in canon beyond DEC-33's three points.
openQuestions.todayInOldUI: A statement page (S8, UI-17a) says what publication is and that the operator publishes for now; it has no publish control.

options.option: Adopt the archived five steps as the design input, re-derived for DEC-72 (case as a production, owner signs), and design them now while the placeholder ships
options.tradeoffs: Uses reasoned, adversarially reviewed work; building still waits for DEC-33's trigger.

options.option: Design only the placeholder now and leave the steps for when the trigger fires
options.tradeoffs: Least work; risks the redesign's layout not leaving room for a heavy ceremony.

options.option: Ask Bob to lift DEC-33 for the redesign
options.tradeoffs: Lets members publish without the operator; brings forward REC-15 and a large body of work.

openQuestions.recommendation: The first option: design the five steps on paper so the layout carries their weight, and ship the placeholder text DEC-33 describes until the trigger fires.
openQuestions.whoDecides: Bob, if the steps become requirements or DEC-33 is reopened; Design for the placeholder wording within DEC-33.

ruled.decided: There is no placeholder: the ceremony and its pre-flight are designed and built in the redesign, in five steps re-derived for DEC-72 (step three discloses any unresolved record contradiction and asks consent for any source identity revealed), and an owner signs in the browser with a registered browser-held key producing the same sshsig signature. A published case may rest on a co-attested Grade B capture, each document's grade and co-attestation disclosed; one whose co-attestation failed may be published only by an attributed acknowledgement and is marked 'self-attested only' (DEC-81). Grade A and further co-witnesses are deferred, their options documented in GRADE-A-CAPTURE.md (DEC-81 item 4).
ruled.title: The publication ceremony

openQuestions.question: Does the project workspace show grades and strength, given the legacy UI hides grades there (UI-16 note) while canon says strength is shown rather than hidden?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Showing strength is the core defence against over-claiming; hiding it in the place members work may undercut that.
openQuestions.whereTheCanonStops: Case Making section 4a; legacy app.html (not canon)
openQuestions.context: Strength is how well a question's answer is supported: a pair (weakest captured document, weakest connection) with testimony beside it, never one score. The project workspace lists the questions and actions inside a project; the old interface deliberately showed no strength there.

canonSays.says: The tool should make a supported case easy and an unsupported one hard to state, visible in the surface: 'strength shown rather than hidden, exclusions named rather than dropped'.
Strength is derived, never stated: a pair of independent measurements with testimony beside them, never composed into one value.
A project declares the strength its work requires (its bar); publishing is refused when a load-bearing leg falls below it.
A project is a container and an inquiry a claim structure; the workspace 'shows NO strength, NO grade and NO conclusion', and a test asserts no grade letter appears.

openQuestions.whyOpen: Canon wants strength visible, and each project declares a bar strength is measured against, yet the screen listing a project's questions hides it. The old reason (a project is a container, a question a claim structure) is an interface choice, not a ruling; the research left open where the line falls between '3 questions live here' and 'one is at grade C'. Showing it in a list must still avoid a single summary figure (DEC-44).
openQuestions.todayInOldUI: The workspace lists questions with no strength or grade; strength appears only on each question's own page.

options.option: Show each question's pair against the project's bar in the list (e.g. 'capture B, connection C; bar B/B'), unrated and undetermined stated
options.tradeoffs: Makes over-claiming visible where work happens; a busier list, and must never collapse into one badge.

options.option: Show only whether each question meets the project's bar (meets / short on connection / undetermined), with the pair one click away
options.tradeoffs: Simple and tied to what matters for publishing; a met/not-met can read like a score.

options.option: Keep the workspace grade-free
options.tradeoffs: Clean container view; contradicts Case Making §4a's 'shown rather than hidden'.

openQuestions.recommendation: The first option: show the pair per question beside the project's bar, because the bar is the project's own declaration and the canon asks strength to be seen.
openQuestions.whoDecides: Design, within Case Making §4a and DEC-44; the old UI note is not canon, so no ruling is needed unless Design proposes hiding strength.

ruled.decided: The project workspace shows strength: each question shows its capture and connection badges (with testimony beside them when an account is part of the answer) and one plain phrase against the project's bar, such as 'Short on connection · bar B/B', 'Undetermined' named with its reason, never one combined score. Every scale follows the measures map Bob approved (letters grade evidence, bars show progress, weights mark acts), docs/development/ux-substrate/measures-map.html, rendered at https://claude.ai/artifact/TfqcXNaJQ86SZzUA8Xn6Ni.
ruled.title: Strength and grades in the project workspace

openQuestions.question: What is the one visual treatment and voice of UNDETERMINED, and how does it differ from 'withheld', 'unrated', 'not looked' and 'refused'?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: It appears in many unrelated places and must be identical everywhere, or members learn to ignore it.
openQuestions.context: 'Undetermined' is the system's honest 'we do not know, and here is why': an unchecked link, an unstated document date, an incomputable strength. It appears in many unrelated places. Nearby states mean different things: withheld (exists, not yours to see), unrated (nothing graded yet), never looked (nobody searched), refused (the system declined an act).

canonSays.says: A display primitive rendered 'identically everywhere', in at least six places; 'first-class and must be STATED, never invented past and never dressed as an error'; 'One visual treatment, one voice: what we do not know, and why we do not know it.'
Something out of view is stated only as an incompleteness: the member learns something is missing, never what it is (withheld).
An ungraded member is inert and named; an axis with no graded member is 'unrated' and says it rests on nothing, distinct from 'undetermined'.
Look states are looked-absent, looked-indeterminate, partial, present and never-looked; a missing look has a cause (pre-log, purged, never looked).

openQuestions.whyOpen: The canon fixes the principle (one look, one voice, with the reason) but no visual treatment or wording exists, and it does not say how the four neighbours differ visibly. The risk runs both ways: if all five look alike, members cannot tell 'nobody looked' from 'we could not tell'; if undetermined looks like an error, members learn to ignore it.
openQuestions.todayInOldUI: A tinted 'undetermined' badge, but the same badge style also marks 'no grade yet', so undetermined and unrated look alike.
related: Q5, Q8 (strength and plan support status reuse it)

options.option: One component with a fixed mark and a mandatory 'because…' line, plus four distinct sibling treatments (withheld, unrated, never looked, refused), each with its own fixed sentence pattern
options.tradeoffs: Clear and teachable; needs a small, strict vocabulary and discipline in every surface.

options.option: One neutral 'gap' family with a colour-free text label for each kind
options.tradeoffs: Accessible and calm; differences rest on reading, easier to miss.

openQuestions.recommendation: The first option: one undetermined component that always carries its reason, and four visibly different neighbours with fixed wording.
openQuestions.whoDecides: Design: §U already sets the principle; the treatment and wording are the designer's within it.

ruled.decided: 'Undetermined' is one component with a fixed mark and a line that always says 'because…', the same everywhere. 'Withheld', 'Unrated', 'Nobody looked' and 'Refused' each have their own visibly different treatment and one fixed sentence pattern, never shared with each other or with Undetermined. None is dressed as an error, and all are written as named terms (DEC-82). The exact marks and wording are the redesign's, within this rule.
ruled.title: “Undetermined” and its four neighbours

openQuestions.question: How does the rung ladder look and feel so a member senses weight before acting, especially the attested and irreversible rungs?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Weight flattening is named as a doctrine failure wearing a usability improvement.
openQuestions.context: Every act carries a 'rung' naming its weight: reversible, reasoned (needs a written reason), terminal, attested (signed, cannot be undone silently) and irreversible (publishing). The aim is that a member feels how heavy an act is before taking it, so dismissing a note and publishing a case never feel like the same click.

canonSays.says: 'Rung' names the weight of an act; the sequence release → … → publish is the 'path to publication'. This settles the naming conflict the substrate recorded.

'Weight flattening' is 'a doctrine failure wearing a usability improvement'; the ladder is 'a property of every act, visible and escalating, learned once and read everywhere'; the top rung carries its own ceremony: 'one thing to learn, two things to feel'.
Attestation can be corrected, but only by a further dated, signed act, never silently; publishing is irreversible and corrections move forward as editions.
The plane publishes each act's rung; 57 ops are still graded 'undetermined' and are to be reassigned by BOB.

openQuestions.whyOpen: K356 settles the word; the look and feel is undesigned. The canon wants weight felt yet also one act shape (choose, pre-flight, reason, receipt), and does not say what escalates with each rung: friction, colour, confirmation, a separate screen. 57 acts have no rung yet, so the design must handle unknown weight.
openQuestions.todayInOldUI: Act dialogs show a five-rung 'How heavy this act is' ladder with the act's own rung lit, worded 'at X weight', which collides with the plane's separate meaning of weight.

options.option: Escalating friction by rung: reversible acts inline; reasoned open a reason field; terminal and attested a full dialog stating what cannot be silently undone; irreversible only through the ceremony
options.tradeoffs: The hand feels the difference; heavier acts are slower, which is the point.

options.option: Same dialog for all, with the ladder shown and the current rung highlighted
options.tradeoffs: Consistent and easy to build; the difference is read rather than felt, the flattening the canon warns against.

openQuestions.recommendation: The first option, with the rung's name on the button, and an undetermined-rung act treated as reasoned until BOB assigns it.
openQuestions.whoDecides: Design, within Interaction Constructs rev. 0.2 and K356; BOB assigns the 57 missing rungs (affordances R27).

ruled.decided: Friction is kept as low as possible so the tool fades and the work stays in focus, while members still feel the weight of their work and the finality of some steps; cues rich in information show state, relationships, context, progression and the acts available; everything is self-evident to newcomers and intuitive to experienced members; and a heavier act slows the member down, even for a moment. Friction follows the rung: a reversible act happens inline; a reasoned act opens a reason field in place; a terminal or attested act opens a full dialog stating what ends or cannot be silently undone, and who signs; an irreversible act goes only through the ceremony. Every act's button shows its rung's name and weight mark, and an act whose rung is not yet set is treated as reasoned. The 57 acts that had no rung have Bob's (26 reversible, 29 reasoned, 2 terminal, DEC-88). Six judgement calls carry high friction whatever their rung: choosing a person's attribution, sharing a lead, registering a subject and setting the group's strength bar open the full dialog stating their effect; approving a filing is terminal and has it already; having the assistant work an objective, the lightest of the six, opens its reason field in place with the run's budget and scope beside it. A heavy consequence is not a new rung.
ruled.title: How the weight of an act is felt

openQuestions.question: Where does a member record why something is (or is not) significant enough to escalate, given no significance field is allowed?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Significance is the point where policy preference most tempts; requirements forbid scores, so the judgment lives only in acts.
openQuestions.whereTheCanonStops: Functional Architecture Layer 2 Function 4; conformance R8
openQuestions.context: Once a group finds that a government body broke a rule, it must decide whether it is worth pursuing (escalating): a report two days late may not be; a $52.6 million unauthorised transfer is. No significance, severity or priority score may be stored, so the judgement exists only as acts on an escalation.

canonSays.says: 'Not every discrepancy is a violation'; significance is 'human judgment informed by context, scale, pattern, and consequences', the point where the temptation to let policy preferences colour compliance judgement 'is strongest'.

canonSays.source: conformance R8; escalation R19; consequences R11; K12
canonSays.says: No input or answer carries a significance, severity, priority, urgency, rank or score; 'significance is the members' judgment'.
Any joined member may open an escalation from a noncompliant determination; advancing, declining a stage and suspending each need a written reason.

openQuestions.whyOpen: Reasons are recorded once an escalation exists, but the first judgement, deciding not to escalate a noncompliant finding at all, has no act and so leaves no trace; nor does the reasoning for opening one. The ban on a significance field protects neutrality, while the doctrine that decisions are authored and kept argues for somewhere to write why. The canon does not reconcile the two.
openQuestions.todayInOldUI: Nothing: the old interface has no escalation surface.

options.option: Require a free-text reason when opening an escalation, and add a reasoned 'decline to escalate' act on a noncompliant determination
options.tradeoffs: Every judgement leaves an authored trace; a new act, and free text could smuggle in a severity word nobody checks.

options.option: Record the reasoning as a declined or chosen option in the action plan (S11)
options.tradeoffs: One home for 'what we chose and why'; the plan is unbuilt and never published (DEC-25).

options.option: Leave it to discussion outside the record
options.tradeoffs: No new mechanism; the most policy-sensitive judgement goes unrecorded.

openQuestions.recommendation: The first option: a required reason when opening and a reasoned decline act, both prose only, so the judgement is kept without becoming a score.
openQuestions.whoDecides: Bob: adding a decline act and a required reason changes the escalation and conformance requirements and touches Operational Principle 1.

ruled.decided: Whether a matter is worth pursuing is recorded only in acts and their reasons, never in a score. Opening an escalation takes a written reason. 'Decline to escalate' on a live noncompliant determination records, in the member's own words, why the group is not pursuing it now: reasoned, attributed and dated, corrected only forward (a later escalation, opened with its own reason, supersedes it and both stay readable). In an action plan, not pursuing a matter is an option declined with a short reason. No field, value or vocabulary for significance, severity, priority, urgency or rank exists anywhere. Any joined member who may open an escalation may decline one.
ruled.title: Where the judgement to pursue a matter, or not, is recorded

openQuestions.question: What does the action plan surface (S11) look like: options, dependencies, deadlines, resources, outcome branches, declined options, and support status on every element?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Impacting has no working process; a plan that hid a hypothetical premise would be the over-claiming failure.
openQuestions.context: When a group finds that an agency broke a rule, it must decide what to do: records requests, referrals, public comment, media, litigation support. The action plan (surface S11) would lay out options, order, deadlines, resources, what follows each outcome, and the options rejected. Each step taken becomes an 'action' page, which exists today.
