openQuestions.question: How does the directory, cross-group discussion and 'working on' signalling appear, if at all, inside CivicOS?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Design Requirements 9-10 require them; no module holds them.
openQuestions.context: The broader Believe in Oakland network expects groups to find each other's published work in a public directory, to discuss across groups in a forum, and to post optional 'working on' signals saying what they are investigating. These sit between groups rather than inside one group's copy of CivicOS.

canonSays.says: A self-hosted Discourse forum 'serves as the operational hub for cross-group discussion'; 'no single platform is essential'; groups host work where they choose.
believeinoakland.org hosts 'a searchable directory of all published work products', with a submission form, no pre-approval, compliance status and visible community flags, and a downloadable mirror.
'Working on' signals are 'lightweight directory entries. Optional, anonymous-compatible, no ownership implied'; 'No group owns an issue.'
The directory and cross-group discussion: 'no built surface serves the directory'.
Acts that are visible outside must say so at the point of the act.

openQuestions.whyOpen: The requirements place the directory and forum on network sites outside CivicOS, but no module or canon text says whether CivicOS itself submits to, reads from or links to them, so the use cases have no requirement. A 'working on' signal publishes a group's interest, which DR-13's tell discipline treats as an outward act that must be flagged, and 'anonymous-compatible' is undefined for a group identified by its public slug.
openQuestions.todayInOldUI: Nothing.

options.option: Keep all three outside CivicOS; CivicOS only offers a 'submit to directory' link after publishing and a 'find related work' link out.
options.tradeoffs: Respects DR-9 and keeps scope small; the experience is split across sites.

options.option: CivicOS submits a published case's metadata to the directory itself and shows its directory status and flags inside.
options.tradeoffs: Smooth for members; needs a directory service and requirements, and couples the product to one site.

options.option: Add an in-product 'working on' act with an explicit tell warning, posting to the directory.
options.tradeoffs: Serves the Roadmap's handoff pattern; publishes interest and needs anonymity rules.

openQuestions.recommendation: Bob should first decide whether these are in CivicOS's scope at all; the smallest honest step is option one, with a tell warning on any link that submits.
openQuestions.whoDecides: Bob: scope and requirements (whether CivicOS owns any of the network's shared functions) are his.

brief.settledBy: Not settled. Nearby rulings only: DEC-92's origin mark for another group's work ('still more to decide later'); K600 (c): joint action with another group 'recorded and deferred until a coalition asks'; Action design D1: a partner group outside the instance may be an action's addressee. Publication §9 still: 'no built surface serves the directory'.
brief.title: Does CivicOS itself connect to the network's directory, forum and 'working on' signals?
brief.decision: Do the Believe in Oakland network's shared functions (the public directory of published work, the cross-group forum and 'working on' signals) stay outside CivicOS, with at most links out? Or does CivicOS submit to them and read from them?
brief.whyYours: Scope and requirements: whether CivicOS takes on any of the network's shared functions is Bob's.
context: The network expects groups to find each other's published work in a searchable directory on believeinoakland.org (Design Requirement 10) and to talk across groups on a self-hosted Discourse forum (DR 9). Groups may also post 'working on' signals, which the Roadmap describes as 'lightweight directory entries. Optional, anonymous-compatible, no ownership implied' (§11). No CivicOS module or requirement serves any of these.

A 'working on' signal publishes a group's interest before any case exists. That is an outward act, and DR 13 requires such acts to say so at the moment they are taken. The Roadmap's 'anonymous-compatible' is undefined for a group whose public identity is its name.

Example: after publishing a case on parking-citation revenue, a member wants it listed in the directory, and wants to know whether another neighbourhood group is looking at the same contracts. Today she leaves CivicOS, fills in the directory's web form and searches the forum by hand.
alreadySettled: No single platform is essential, and groups host their work where they choose (DR 9).
Directory: submission with no pre-approval, compliance status, visible community flags, downloadable mirror (DR 10). 'No group owns an issue' (Roadmap §11).
Acts visible outside must say so at the act (DR 13). Nothing non-public leaves by a system path (DEC-31; K597 (5)).
Another group's work carries an origin mark (DEC-92). Joint action is deferred until a coalition asks (K600 (c)).

options.label: A
options.name: Outside, with links out
options.whatTheMemberSees: After publishing: 'Submit to the network directory', which opens the directory's form with the public case address filled in and says 'This goes to a public website'. Also a 'Find related work' link to the directory's search.
options.gains: Respects DR 9, keeps scope small, and needs no directory service.
options.costs: The experience stays split across sites.

options.label: B
options.name: CivicOS submits and shows the status
options.whatTheMemberSees: A 'List in directory' act at publication; the case page shows its directory status and any community flags.
options.gains: Smooth for members.
options.costs: Needs the directory to exist as a service, plus new requirements, and ties the product to one site.

options.label: C
options.name: A 'working on' act inside CivicOS
options.whatTheMemberSees: 'Tell the network we are working on this', with the warning 'This tells the public your group is investigating ...'.
options.gains: Supports coordination between groups early.
options.costs: Publishes interest early, and needs anonymity rules defined first.

brief.recommendation: A, the smallest honest step. Revisit B when the directory exists as a service, and C when a group asks for it, with 'anonymous-compatible' defined first. (Recommendation, not canon; whether the directory service exists yet is not recorded in the repository.)
howToAnswer: As recommended.
As recommended, and give C a trigger: the first time two groups duplicate an investigation.
B: CivicOS should list cases in the directory itself.
Out of scope entirely: no links either.
brief.ifLeftOpen: UC-005, UC-110 and UC-125 stay without requirements, and members use the network's sites by hand.

openQuestions.question: How are strength, grades and look states explained to the public reader at progressively deeper levels, and in print?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Readers know least; print loses interactivity and must carry the full narrative.
openQuestions.context: Published cases are read by the public, journalists, officials and other groups, who know the least about CivicOS. A case reports each finding's strength on two separate axes (how directly the documents are held, and how strongly the links between them are established), letter grades A-D, and 'look states' saying what was searched and what nobody looked at. Bob wants this explained in layers on screen, and the printed version must carry the whole story without interactivity.

canonSays.says: Interactive story visuals extend to the published surface, 'where readers know the least, so progressive disclosure matters most there. The PRINTED version... is first-class and must carry the full narrative, progressively explained and documented'.
No answer composes a case-level strength: every pair is per member and per axis.
The published case carries scope, completeness, bias acknowledgement, the bar with its words, each member's pair and grounds; undetermined is stated, never filled.
Absence has five states (NEVER_LOOKED, LOOKED_ABSENT, LOOKED_INDETERMINATE, PARTIAL, PRESENT); the completeness statement's search record is designed, not built.
Letters grade evidence, bars show progress, weights mark acts; every grade and bar step opens its meaning on hover, focus or tap; colour marks the scale, never the value.

openQuestions.whyOpen: The canon demands layered explanation and a full printed narrative but defines neither the layers nor the words. Readers expect one overall score, while DEC-44 forbids combining the two axes, so the explanation must teach why there is no single number. The look states cannot yet appear on a published case because the search record is not built, and Bob's principle that print must carry everything that on screen is hidden behind click-overs has no stated order or length limit.
openQuestions.todayInOldUI: The old published page opens the strength section with a paragraph explaining the two axes and the weakest-leg rule, and its print stylesheet prints the in-band notice first, expands every collapsed leg and adds full addresses and hashes to links.

options.option: Three fixed layers: a one-line verdict per finding in words, then the two-axis pair with a short explanation, then the legs, grades and search record; print renders all three in order with a glossary page.
options.tradeoffs: Predictable for readers and print; long printouts for large cases.

options.option: Per-term click-overs from the semantics table on screen, printed as footnotes.
options.tradeoffs: Reuses one source of truth; footnote-heavy print.

openQuestions.recommendation: Use the three layers with semantics-table click-overs, printing all layers plus a one-page glossary; the one-line verdict must state each axis and never a single score.
openQuestions.whoDecides: Design, within Bob's stated principles and DEC-44; Bob only if a single summary line per finding is thought to risk composing the pair.

brief.settledBy: Largely settled. DEC-82 gives readers' explanations their words ('an answer is only as strong as the weakest thing it depends on'; a grade says 'how easily someone else could check it, never whether it is true'; what we don't know is shown), with one form per scale, every mark opening to its plain question, and colour marking the scale, never the value. DEC-82 also approved a one-line verdict against the bar in the members' workspace ('Meets the bar', 'Short on connection'). DEC-81: each document's grade and co-attestation is disclosed. DEC-76 and DEC-84 (12): a contradiction is disclosed one level deep. DEC-86: the five 'gap' treatments. Left: the order and length of print (Design's), and whether readers also get the verdict line.
brief.title: How a published case explains its strength to the public, on screen and in print
brief.decision: Should a published case give readers, for each finding, the same one-line verdict against the bar that members see in their workspace (for example 'Meets the bar' or 'Short on connection'), above the detailed grades? And does the printed edition carry every layer, however long it gets?
brief.whyYours: Mostly Design's, within Bob's principles: explanation in layers, and print 'first-class' carrying 'the full narrative'. Bob's piece is whether a single verdict line risks reading as one combined score, which DEC-44 forbids. He approved such a line for members (DEC-82) but not yet for the public.
context: Public readers (residents, journalists, officials) know least about CivicOS. Each finding has two grades, capture (how well the documents are held) and connection (how firmly the links are established), a bar the project set, and statements about what was searched and what nobody looked at. Readers expect one overall score, and the canon forbids one (DEC-44).

Example: a reporter opens a published case. Layer 1: 'Finding 3: the city spent $2.1M outside the measure's categories. Meets the bar.' Layer 2: 'capture B (co-attested), connection B; bar B/B', each opening its meaning. Layer 3: the documents, the links and the search record. The printed edition carries the same three layers in order, plus a one-page glossary.
The 'what nobody looked at' statements cannot appear on a published case until the search record is built (Publication §9).
alreadySettled: No composed case-level or finding-level score: every pair is per finding and per axis (DEC-44; publication R26).
The published case carries scope, completeness, bias acknowledgement, the bar with its words, and each finding's pair and grounds; 'undetermined' is stated, never filled (publication R10, R28).
DEC-82's frame, principles and three sentences. DEC-86's five treatments (Undetermined, Withheld, Unrated, Nobody looked, Refused).

Grade and co-attestation disclosed per document, with 'self-attested only' where co-attestation failed (DEC-81). Contradictions disclosed one level deep (DEC-84 (12)), and a hidden-side conflict highlighted without naming the other project (DEC-85).
Print is first-class and carries the full narrative (UI-KICKOFF refinements, Bob 2026-07-28).

options.label: A
options.name: Verdict line, then the pair, then the detail
options.whatTheMemberSees: As in the example; print carries all three layers and a glossary.
options.gains: Readers get the answer first, in the same words members use.
options.costs: A single phrase could be read as a score, which is reduced by naming which axis is short.

options.label: B
options.name: Pairs only, no verdict line
options.whatTheMemberSees: 'capture B · connection C · bar B/B', each opening its meaning; in print, footnotes.
options.gains: Nothing resembles a score.
options.costs: Readers must compare grades against the bar themselves, and many will not.

brief.recommendation: A. It reuses the phrase Bob approved for members, measures only against the project's own bar, names the short axis, and so combines nothing. Print carries every layer with no length limit, and Design sets the order and typography. (Recommendation, not canon.)
howToAnswer: As recommended.
B: no verdict line for the public.
A, but print only the first two layers plus an address for the rest.
brief.ifLeftOpen: Design builds the reader's layers from DEC-82 and leaves the verdict line out until Bob says otherwise.

openQuestions.question: What does placing a 'litigation hold' do in CivicOS: which routine deletions does it suspend, and for which material? Who may place it and lift it, and what do members see while it is on?

brief.settledBy: Open, and marked as Bob's. build/plan/action-fold/t18-entries.md: the litigation-hold reminder 'waits for the hold's act, whose design (what a hold suspends, who lifts it) is Bob's doctrine'. draft-T18-recut: 'N-A19 (the litigation-hold item, once the hold's act is designed, Bob's doctrine)'. K624 (5) moved it to T19. Settled parts: K613 (2): the reminder 'is not repeated unless the member asks; the hold may be cleared when responding to it, and if not cleared it stays open until cleared'. DEC-61 (2026-08-06): 'THEREFORE THE PURGE MUST BE SUSPENDABLE — a litigation hold'.
brief.title: The litigation hold: what it stops, and who starts and ends it
brief.decision: What does placing a 'litigation hold' do in CivicOS: which routine deletions does it suspend, and for which material? Who may place it and lift it, and what do members see while it is on?
brief.whyYours: Doctrine with legal consequences for the group. DEC-61 set the deletion rules, and the canon warns that getting the hold wrong 'inverts the protection into liability'. The Action design hands this to Bob by name.
context: Some material is deleted by design. An assistant session's transcript stays on the member's own device, is deleted after a set time and again when the case publishes (DEC-61), because such 'internal notes ... need to be protected from subpoenas'. Deleting on a fixed schedule is defensible; deleting once a lawsuit is expected is destruction of evidence. So the canon requires the routine deletion to be suspendable, which is a litigation hold, but no such act exists.

The Action design adds the trigger. When a member marks a reply as legal pressure (a threat to sue, a subpoena, a demand to preserve records), an administrator gets a to-do: 'Consider a litigation hold.' Bob ruled that the item is never repeated and stays open until it is cleared. With no hold to place, the item has no way to be resolved, so it was not built (moved to T19).

Example: the city attorney writes to a group demanding it preserve everything about its report on towing contracts. Paula marks the letter 'legal', and her administrator Sam sees 'Consider a litigation hold'. What should pressing 'Place hold' do? Stop transcript deletion on every member's device? For this project only, or the whole group? Who can lift it, and must they give a reason? None of this is decided.
alreadySettled: Transcripts are device-local, deleted after a set time and at publication, never in the record store; the deletion must be suspendable (DEC-61; INVESTIGATIVE-SESSION.md §14a).
Only a member marks pressure, and the legal kind is one of four (actions R48; K597 (1)).
The hold reminder is not repeated unless asked, may be cleared when answered, and otherwise stays open (K613 (2)).
Heavy acts get a full dialog (DEC-87, DEC-88); with no outside channel, a hold reaches a device when its member next opens the product (DEC-94 (3)).

options.label: A
options.name: A narrow hold on DEC-61's deletions, per project
options.whatTheMemberSees: Sam places a hold on the towing project, with a reason. Members' devices stop deleting that project's session transcripts, and a band reads 'Litigation hold since 3 Oct: nothing in this project is deleted on schedule.' Lifting it is a reasoned administrator act.
options.gains: Fits exactly what DEC-61 requires, and other projects keep their protection.
options.costs: Project scope may miss related material in other projects.

options.label: B
options.name: A group-wide hold on all scheduled deletion
options.whatTheMemberSees: A band across the whole app; every scheduled deletion stops.
options.gains: The simplest to explain and the safest legally.
options.costs: Keeps internal notes for unrelated work, exposing them to the very subpoena risk DEC-61 guards against.

options.label: C
options.name: Record the decision; preserve by hand
options.whatTheMemberSees: A reasoned act 'Hold considered: placed / not placed, because ...', plus a checklist of what to preserve.
options.gains: No new machinery.
options.costs: Device deletions keep running unless every member acts.

brief.recommendation: A. It matches the one deletion DEC-61 says must be suspendable, keeps protection for unrelated work, and records who placed and lifted the hold and why. It should be a heavy act placed by an administrator. Counsel's view would be worth having, and nothing here is legal advice. (Recommendation, not canon.)
howToAnswer: As recommended.
B: group-wide, always.
A, but any member may place it; only administrators lift it.
Let's take this up with a lawyer first.
brief.ifLeftOpen: The legal-pressure mark is built, but no to-do follows it and no hold exists. Transcripts keep being deleted on schedule even after a legal threat is recorded.

openQuestions.question: Which plain word does member-facing text use for a single thing the record holds (a captured document, a written observation, a question, a finding), now that Bob has retired 'bundle'?

brief.settledBy: Open. K106 (Bob, 2026-09-26): 'the word "bundle" is outdated'. next.md N71: 'BOB asks Bob which word the member-facing text uses.' It is listed among 'Bob's first' in draft-T18.md §6. The UX inventory's glossary drafts 'Document' for evidence items only, and that is not approved.
brief.title: The everyday word for one item in the record (replacing 'bundle')
brief.decision: Which plain word does member-facing text use for a single thing the record holds (a captured document, a written observation, a question, a finding), now that Bob has retired 'bundle'?
brief.whyYours: It is member vocabulary, and Bob retired the word himself. It is the same kind of call as 'Noticed' (K356).
context: Internally, everything the record holds is a 'bundle' with an id: a captured page, a transcription, a question, a finding. Bob called the word outdated. New canon and requirements avoid it, but some member-facing messages still say it, and the code keeps it as an internal name.

The difficulty is that 'bundle' covers two kinds of thing: evidence (documents and observations) and analysis (questions and findings). The inventory's draft glossary uses 'Document' for evidence only.
Example: Maya opens a link to something in a project she cannot see. Today: 'No such bundle.' The message must not reveal whether the thing exists, or what type it is (DEC-36; membership R88).
alreadySettled: 'Bundle' is not used in new canon or requirement text; internal names change only with a migration BOB schedules (K106; N71).
A hidden item answers exactly as an absent one, and reveals nothing about itself (DEC-36; connections R20; membership R88).

options.label: A
options.name: The specific name where known, 'item' otherwise
options.whatTheMemberSees: 'document', 'observation', 'question' or 'finding' wherever the type is known and visible; 'This item does not exist, or you cannot see it' where it is not.
options.gains: Always accurate, and never reveals a hidden type.
options.costs: 'Item' is bland.

options.label: B
options.name: 'Record entry'
options.whatTheMemberSees: 'No such record entry.'
options.gains: Sounds official.
options.costs: 'The record' already means the whole working record, so it invites confusion.

options.label: C
options.name: 'Document' for everything
options.whatTheMemberSees: 'No such document', even for a question.
options.gains: Familiar.
options.costs: Wrong for questions and findings.

brief.recommendation: A: the specific name wherever the type is known, 'item' only where it is unknown or must stay hidden, and 'Document' for evidence, as the glossary drafts. (Recommendation, not canon.)
howToAnswer: As recommended.
As recommended, but use 'entry' instead of 'item'.
Show me the five places members see the word today.
brief.ifLeftOpen: Member-facing messages keep 'bundle' where they have it, and the redesign picks words case by case.

openQuestions.question: Should the current member app (the old interface) get small patches for the paths that now fail, with a plain 'not available here yet' where features are missing? Or does everything wait for the redesign, even where members now hit refusals with no way forward?

brief.settledBy: Open, and marked Bob's (UX): next.md N241 ('a UX question for Bob'), N371 ('UX, Bob's with N144/N241'), N389 ('UX, Bob's with N371'); N-A13 (the old app's action form writes a counterparty shape actions R9 refuses) 'joins N389'. All are listed under draft-T18.md §6 'Bob's first'. Standing rule: the old app has no requirements and gets no tranche work (K5, K283). K501: 'app.html's publish sends no disclosure, so a case with a standing conflict duty is refused C-120.1 from the app until DEC-80's ceremony step is built; told to Bob.'
brief.title: What the current app does until the redesign arrives
brief.decision: Should the current member app (the old interface) get small patches for the paths that now fail, with a plain 'not available here yet' where features are missing? Or does everything wait for the redesign, even where members now hit refusals with no way forward?
brief.whyYours: It decides what members can do and see in the meantime, and whether effort goes into a screen that is being replaced. That is partly a priority call rather than pure UX, and it is flagged as Bob's in the build plan.
context: The system has moved ahead of the app it serves. Six record types added in T8 (standard, goal, escalation, determination, consequence, aspiration) are missing from the app. A contradiction cannot be resolved from it. A source's consent and publication's disclosures have no screen. The action form writes a counterparty in a shape the system now refuses. Publishing a case that carries an unresolved conflict is refused, because the app sends no disclosure.
The standing rule is that the old app gets no build work, the redesign replaces it, and onboarding waits until the redesign settles (DEC-91).

Example: a member creates a records-request action naming 'City Clerk' and is refused (COUNTERPARTY_REFUSED), because a role and a body are now required. Another tries to publish and is refused (C-120.1), with no place in the app to give the disclosure. It is not recorded whether any group uses the old app for real work today.
alreadySettled: The old app has no requirements and gets no tranche work (K5, K283).
The ceremony and its disclosures are designed and built in the redesign, with no placeholder (DEC-80).
Onboarding is deferred until the redesign is stable (DEC-91).

options.label: A
options.name: Fix what is broken; label what is missing
options.whatTheMemberSees: The counterparty form asks for role and body. Publishing offers the disclosure step. Missing features say 'Not available in this version yet'.
options.gains: No dead ends for anyone using the app now.
options.costs: Small exceptions to the 'no work on the old app' rule.

options.label: B
options.name: Wait for the redesign
options.whatTheMemberSees: The app unchanged; refusals with no way forward.
options.gains: All effort goes to the redesign.
options.costs: Members hit dead ends if anyone is using it.

options.label: C
options.name: Bring the app up to date
options.whatTheMemberSees: Every missing surface added.
options.gains: Full use now.
options.costs: Substantial work that will be thrown away.

brief.recommendation: A if any group relies on the app before the redesign ships. B if no group is live yet. (Recommendation, not canon; whether a group is live is not recorded in the repository.)
howToAnswer: A.
B: nobody is using it yet.
A, but only the publish disclosure.
brief.ifLeftOpen: The old app stays as it is: some action and publication paths fail with refusals, and the missing record types stay invisible there.

openQuestions.question: The approved plan page heads its first section “Subjects”. Should members see “Subjects” there, or “Matters”, given that “Subject” already names something else in the product?

brief.question: The word 'Subject' now means two things. Keep 'Subjects' on the plan page, or call them 'Matters'?
brief.title: What members call the things a plan is about: “Subjects” or “Matters”
brief.decision: The approved plan page heads its first section “Subjects”. Should members see “Subjects” there, or “Matters”, given that “Subject” already names something else in the product?
brief.whyYours: It is a word every member reads on the plan page, and choosing member vocabulary has been yours (“Noticed” for the queue's unjudged items, K356; retiring “bundle”).
brief.context:
A plan is about one or more things the group suspects or has determined, for example “The city's certification of the bond measure” or “Late release of council minutes”. Each is either suspected (an open question the group is still investigating) or determined (a member has judged the government act compliant, noncompliant or unclear against a standard). The plan page lists them first, each with how well it is shown: established, short, or hypothetical.

Elsewhere in the product a “Subject” is already something the record knows by name: a person in a public role, an office, a place, a law or a thing. The Subjects screen lists, for example, “City Council (office)”. A member who meets both could reasonably read a plan as being about an office rather than about something the office did.

The Action canon's own prose already calls them matters (“one plan may address several related matters”). The requirements' internal term is “subject”, which members never need to see, whichever word you choose.

The canon speaks of a plan's “matters” (BIO_Action_v0_1.md §3).

options.costs: A small change to the approved sketch.

brief.recommendation: A, “Matters”: it removes the clash, the canon already uses it, and it reads as well for a success as for a breach.

brief.whyYours: An approved sketch binds the redesign; a draft only informs it. Which screens are fixed at this stage is a UX decision.
brief.context:
Starting and sending (views/start-and-send.html) is what a member sees on starting a chosen option: a preview of what the action will say (addressee, dates with their basis, what it rests on) and what it would refuse. It shows the case you ruled on: an action asserting a breach while the matter is unestablished is refused by default, with “Proceed with this reason”, after which the action and everything prepared from it say “rests on an unestablished premise”. It then shows a message drafted by the assistant, which the member edits, approves and sends by their own hand, recording the sending.

The matter page (views/matter-page.html) gathers everything about one government act: its determination, consequences, escalation stage and the actions taken on it. The member's path through acting (PATH.md) does not name this page, and it overlaps the existing Escalation and Standards screens.

The queue sketch (views/surfaces.html) shows the new queue items: a checkpoint due (the group's own to-do), a proposed escalation stage, and an action's deadline passed (a condition, told once). It also shows a “consider a litigation hold” item, which is not built until T19 and whose meaning is question 31. The approved plan page is at views/plan-page.html for comparison.

What each Action screen must and must never show (PATH.md §3, in the approved design record).
The override pattern: refuse by default, a member may proceed openly with a reason, disclosed on everything prepared (BIO_Action_v0_1.md §4 rule 2).

options.label: A
options.name: Fix all three
options.whatTheMemberSees: The redesign follows all four sketches.
options.gains: The designer has a complete, fixed reference for the Action layer.
options.costs: Fixes a matter page whose place among the existing screens is unsettled, and a queue item whose meaning is still open (31).

options.label: B
options.name: Fix starting and sending only
options.whatTheMemberSees: The start preview, the override and the draft-approve-send flow as sketched; the matter page and queue items as the designer settles them within PATH.md's rules.
options.gains: Fixes the one flow that carries doctrine (the override and the member's own sending).
options.costs: The other two wait for the designer.

options.label: C
options.name: Fix none
options.whatTheMemberSees: The designer works from PATH.md and the requirements alone.
options.gains: Most freedom for the redesign.
options.costs: The override flow, which you ruled on, has no fixed picture.

brief.recommendation: B: fix starting and sending, which carries your override ruling; leave the matter page and the queue items to the designer, the queue sketch to be revisited once question 31 is ruled.
